A1.justification: Both readable, ten-page PDFs describe the same AnyAttack study. However, both end with references and omit the appendices cited for Flickr30K results, implementation details and additional commercial-model examples. Those materials cannot be compared.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, multimodal classification, captioning and commercial-model attack results in Tables 1–4, plus ablation and efficiency results in Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the frozen encoder, noise decoder, K-augmentation, temperature schedule, auxiliary models and cosine/bidirectional fine-tuning objectives. The new strategy-comparison table does not introduce a different algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions specify LAION-400M pre-training, MSCOCO/Flickr30K/SNLI-VE downstream coverage and ImageNet-1K clean images. The three tasks and open-source/commercial model families remain the same; v3's precise commercial model names add documentation.

E2.justification: All supplied benchmark tables retain the same AttackVLM-ii/-it, SASD-WS-Cos/-MSE and SU-Cos/-MSE comparators. However, the missing Flickr30K results prevent checking comparator membership in that explicitly referenced comparison.

E3.justification: The stated training budgets, sample counts, perturbation bound and downstream evaluation settings match. Section 4.5 changes unspecified 'relevant' responses to explicitly counting 'highly and partially relevant' responses. Because v2 omits the answer choices and detailed appendix setup, clarification versus a scoring-rule revision cannot be established.

E4.justification: The supplied pre-training, auxiliary-model and loss ablations, efficiency analysis and commercial example are unchanged in substance. Both versions reference additional commercial examples in unavailable appendices, preventing a complete comparison of case studies.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. R@Mean remains an average across retrieval metrics, not an estimate of run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: All 77 result rows match between v2 Tables 1–4 and v3 Tables 2–5, and Figures 3–5 retain their findings. For example, classification accuracy remains 44.8 and commercial ASRs remain 31 and 38. Unavailable Flickr30K results and additional appendix examples prevent confirming complete result-level invariance.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. New Table 1 summarizes the existing supervision strategies and AnyAttack objective; it adds no substantive mathematical assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and first contribution reframe flexibility from allowing any image to serve as a target to transforming any image into an attack vector 'targeting any desired output across different VLMs.' This broadens the stated output scope, while the central pre-training/fine-tuning contribution and evaluation claims remain.

C2.justification: The shortened jailbreak discussion removes the explicit mechanism explanation that jailbreaks influence the LLM while image attacks typically leave it largely undisturbed. Section 4's interpretations of pre-training, auxiliary models, losses and transferability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o mini, API use and the full commercial-evaluation answer choices. It replaces the direct repository link with a project-page link and removes the explicit model-weight release statement. These are documentation changes, not evidence that weights were withdrawn or experiments rerun.

R1.justification: v3 removes the cited works by Bagdasaryan et al. on indirect instruction injection, Jia et al. on ALIGN, and Zou et al. on transferable language-model attacks. The jailbreak background is condensed; positioning against AttackVLM and the self-supervised novelty argument remain.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and author/affiliation information, rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, condenses jailbreak background, adds acknowledgements and corrects table cross-references. Most method/results prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-row strategy-formulation table and renumbers existing result tables. Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 6 with reflowed response text, Figure 5 is reduced in size, and Figure 1's caption changes. Existing plots and result-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Exact commercial model names, answer choices and corrected table references improve transparency. However, the broader 'any desired output' framing receives no additional validation in the unchanged supplied results, which include partial relevance as success. These competing effects, together with unavailable appendix evidence, prevent a reliable paper-level net-quality judgment.
